messages:
emily: Hey all — high-priority billing escalation from customer 'BlueShip'. They say a streaming call they cancelled mid-generation was billed for a large finalization chunk (≈11.8k tokens). Session id: sess_9f3c. They have invoice #INV-4892 showing the bump.

raj: Ack. Do we have the request_id / route / model? Any SDK vs raw HTTP? :eyes:

emily: They used our JS SDK v0.9.1, model:redwood-pro-13b, route `/v1/chat/stream`. Customer says they hit ctrl-c in the browser and the client emitted the SSE close event. SDK logs show a client-side websocket.close and a 0-byte final frame. No explicit 'cancel' API call.

zane: Hmm. If the client closed the connection, server may still have processed tokens then emitted a finalization event that our metering job later attributed. Could be race where post-close finalization arrived and our dedupe window didn't drop it. Can you paste the raw SSE frames from the customer?

emily: Pasting sanitized frames below (customer redacted some PII):

```
:keepalive
event: chunk
data: {"id":"sess_9f3c","delta":"...tokenized piece..."}

event: chunk
data: {"id":"sess_9f3c","delta":"...more..."}

event: trailer
data: {"id":"sess_9f3c","final_tokens":11824,"status":"complete"}

# client console log shows immediate connection close after receiving the second chunk, before trailer arrives
```

maria: So trailer arrived after client closed? That implies the server finished generation and emitted the trailer which our streamer wrote to the ledger. But normally if connection closed, we still finalize and count tokens. Why is customer disputing — do they expect no charge on client cancel?

emily: Customer expects a partial-charge (only tokens sent to client). They assert their app cancelled before final tokens were realized. Their dashboard (real-time usage) shows ~3.2k tokens for the session, invoice shows 11.8k.

raj: That discrepancy sounds like instrumentation mismatch between real-time dashboard (streams only) and final ledger (includes server-side completed tokens). We need to: 1) confirm what our billing ledger records for that session, 2) confirm dashboard aggregation rules, 3) check whether post-close finalization should be credited/marked differently.

zane: Quick checks: - Look for ingestion times in the streaming shard and the finalization job. If finalization event had server timestamp > client close, ledger will reflect full cost. There is also a dedupe window (30s) for replay protection — if our finalization was ingested after client close and we didn't have a matching prefix checksum, it could be counted as a new session.

emily: I pulled ledger rows: `ledger.stream_events` has three chunk rows + one trailer row with final_tokens=11824; `realtime.metrics` shows cumulative tokens emitted to client: 3208.

maria: Two immediate hypotheses: (A) The trailer was emitted by a downstream fallback model (larger prompt expansion) after re-routing, and our dashboard is only counting tokens up to reroute; or (B) Our streaming agent sometimes coalesces internal sub-steps into a single trailer that reports full tokenization even if many tokens never flowed to the socket.

zane: To test (B), we should repro locally: simulate a client that closes before trailer, and inspect whether our runtime still finalizes with large final_tokens and whether the counter that emits to SSE differs. I can spin a repro with the same model and a long generation seed.

raj: Meanwhile, billing-side: we should put a temporary hold on invoice #INV-4892 and create a credit review for BlueShip. I'll open a support ticket and flag for finance approval. billing-bot: please create ticket and attach trace when ready. :thumbsup:

billing-bot: Created billing case BG-1229 for INV-4892 and assigned to raj. Link: https://billing.redwood/cases/BG-1229

emily: Customer provided raw SDK telemetry: `request_id: r_81c2`, `route: /v1/chat/stream`, `region: us-west-2`. They can reproduce consistently: close after chunk 2, trailer comes later.

zane: Running repro now. Quick note — check the streamer code path: `stream_writer` writes chunks async and the model runner may keep producing tokens until it receives cancel from the runner; if cancel is only propagated when socket close is processed by accept loop, we might already be too late. There's an in-flight buffer that will still be flushed and accounted.

maria: If the policy is that server-completed tokens are billable even if client disconnects, we should ensure docs and dashboard reflect that. But for disputes, we may want to credit the difference if customer expectation mismatch.

emily: BlueShip is a small startup — they asked for a one-off credit while we fix or clarify. They provided consent to share logs with our eng team.

zane: Repro note: I see a trailer row appended by finalizer with `final_tokens=11824` and a separate stream emission counter of 3208. The finalizer runs in a different service and emits a `finalize` event to ledger-service; ledger-service currently trusts the `final_tokens` field from finalizer. If finalizer counts internal speculative tokens (not streamed), that explains the delta.

raj: Action items: 
- zane: produce minimal repro and PR to make finalizer compute streamed_token_count vs final_token_count and write both values to ledger (due EOD).
- emily: open credit request (BG-1229) and keep customer updated; propose a partial credit equal to ledger-final - dashboard-streamed = ~8.6k tokens pending eng confirmation.
- maria: review API docs and add FAQ about client-side cancels and billing behavior.
- raj: finance to hold invoice until BG-1229 resolved.

maria: Also propose adding a flag on ledger entries `count_policy: server_final | streamed_only` so we can support customers wanting streamed-only billing in the future (opt-in). I'll draft a proposal.

emily: Customer replied: thanks, wants credit while you investigate. They provided a second session where the trailer didn't appear at all and dashboard and ledger match — so it's intermittent.

zane: Repro completed: confirmed finalizer receives internal completion token count that includes speculative tokens. PR incoming to split metrics. Also adding a short-term patch: if socket closed and finalizer's first-seen timestamp > socket-closed-ts + 5s, mark ledger `post_close=true` so ops can filter.

raj: Sounds good. For BG-1229 I'll provision a provisional credit of 8.6k tokens pending eng PR merge and product signoff. emily, please confirm with customer.

emily: Confirmed with customer, they accepted provisional credit while we fix. I'll update the ticket and close loop once PR merged. :white_check_mark:

billing-bot: BG-1229 updated: provisional credit 8600 tokens applied to INV-4892; awaiting eng confirmation.

maria: I'll start a doc PR for the FAQ and postmortem once root cause is verified.

zane: PR link: https://git.redwood/eng/streaming/merge_requests/429 — split finalized counts and add post_close annotation. Tests included.

emily: Thanks team — closing loop with BlueShip now. Will reopen if anything regresses.

raj: Great. Long-term, we should evaluate making streamed_token_count the default billing metric or at least offer it as a plan option. Noted for product roadmap.

maria: +1 on plan option. Filing a product ticket.

emily: End of thread.
